topic: Sharp minimax design under bounded pair mismatch. For N=2J labeled units in known pairs with binary fixed potential outcomes and at most s armwise-discordant pairs, optimize jointly over every assignment law and every measurable SATE estimator. Characterize the complete invariant optimal-design face by a polynomial-size orbit game and matching least-favourable-prior dual; give iff certificates for paired, iid-Bernoulli, canonical-mixture, essentially noncanonical, and unique optima. Prove J R*(J,s_J) converges to min(rho,1/2) when s_J/J tends to rho, all-mixed concentration below rho=1/2, and the first-order envelope of o(J^-1)-optimal invariant procedures, while exact finite-minimizer selection is posed as the open J^(2/3)-critical, J^(-4/3)-residual Gamma-limit problem. Supply exact finite randomization-test inversion. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact rational enumeration at J=2,s=1 finds a noncanonical procedure with worst risk below 0.09065 while a dual prior forces every paired/Bernoulli mixture above 0.09102. A shrinking five-type prior, van Trees bound, empirical-SATE transfer, and hard-budget conditioning derive the sharp first-order value min(rho,1/2), with endpoint and degeneracy checks surviving. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: characterize which first-order optimal limiting measures are limits of exact finite minimizers for rho>=1/2, including critical-sequence and smaller-order selection. EARLY KILL TEST: rerun the rational certificate, enumerate J=2,3,4 for every s, and optimize the full finite optimal faces; pivot if exact optimizer selection cannot be distinguished from first-order optimality. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_pairdiscordance_minimax_design.md

open_problems.open_problem: For binary fixed potential outcomes on J known pairs with at most s armwise-discordant pairs, characterize the entire invariant finite-sample minimax face over all assignment laws and measurable SATE estimators, including iff certificates for paired, iid-Bernoulli, canonical-mixture, essentially noncanonical, and unique optima.

source_refs.claim: After proving finite-sample minimaxity under exact permutation invariance, Bai explicitly asks what happens when invariance holds only approximately.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.claim: The unrestricted binary-potential-outcome problem reduces under full unit exchangeability to a low-dimensional experiment and is solved by Bernoulli assignment with nonlinear shrinkage.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Kallus characterizes mixed-strategy minimax designs for structured conditional-mean classes but optimizes a precision criterion rather than unrestricted nonlinear SATE estimators under a hard pair-type budget.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.excerpt: returning outward value brackets, all minimizing design cells, and explicit covariance and selector witnesses

open_problems.why_unsolved: Full exchangeability collapses schedules to global counts, whereas bounded pair mismatch preserves only pair permutations and within-pair swaps and couples the surviving pair types through a hard cardinality constraint. Bai identifies approximate invariance as unresolved, Kallus fixes a variance-based analysis, and the prior saturation proposal leaves open an all-minimizer certificate even after finite symmetry reduction. Here the unrestricted estimator makes the observation kernel nonlinear and introduces zero-mass cells, so a value calculation alone cannot recover the exposed optimal face or distinguish canonical from noncanonical laws. The first missing step is a lossless orbit reduction of both procedure risk and constrained schedules, followed by a dual whose contact equations classify every optimizer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample theorem reducing the problem to a polynomial-size pair-orbit zero-sum game with a matching least-favourable-prior dual and iff complementary-slackness certificates for membership and uniqueness of every named design family.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from the practical role of randomization to a permutation-invariant minimax theorem and then isolates approximate invariance as the next boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact exchangeability makes complete randomization minimax -> pair information leaves only a smaller symmetry group -> a hard mismatch budget demands the exact robust procedure and its full optimal face

method_exemplars.technique: Use endpoint and symmetry reductions, finite minimax duality, and a least-favourable prior whose posterior mean supplies the optimal nonlinear estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is also a joint assignment-estimator minimax characterization for binary finite-population SATE, but its sufficient statistic must retain pair-orbit counts and the mismatch budget.

method_exemplars.technique: Average procedures over a permutation group and use invariance of the parameter class and loss to reduce the minimax decision space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The pair-preserving wreath-product action is the natural replacement for Bai's full permutation group and is the first route to a polynomial orbit game.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent randomized designs as mixed strategies in a convex minimax program and derive support restrictions from the active constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its mixed-strategy geometry is suited to recognizing noncanonical optimal laws, while the new game must additionally optimize unrestricted estimators.

open_problems.open_problem: For sequences s_J/J tending to rho, determine the sharp asymptotic minimax risk and exact limiting optimal-design face, including which first-order-optimal measures are attainable by exact finite minimizers when rho is at least one half and how critical sequences select among them.

source_refs.claim: For unrestricted binary schedules, the paper proves a second-order minimax expansion and shows that standard procedures coincide with the optimum only to first order.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Under an unrestricted bounded-outcome adversary, independent assignment remains optimal, while complete within-pair randomization with pair fixed effects has twice its worst-case MSE.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.claim: Within stratified half-treatment designs under a superpopulation precision criterion, a matched-pair design is optimal, contrasting with Bernoulli optimality under an unrestricted bounded fixed-population criterion.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.excerpt: Each exact program certifies one population size; it does not compare adjacent values or prove tightness of optimizers.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature gives opposite endpoint prescriptions because Bai exploits prognostic pair structure within stratified designs, whereas Hull and Sudijono–Dobriban–Tchetgen Tchetgen protect against unrestricted bounded schedules. A hard discordance fraction interpolates between these endpoints, but no located paper derives its phase transition or optimizer-set limit. The banked multi-arm project independently records that same-size rational saddle certificates do not establish cross-size tightness or convergence. At rho=1/2 the leading objective may be flat, so proving J R*(J,s_J) alone cannot identify which measures are limits of exact finite minimizers. The scalar unrestricted-schedule reduction must be replaced by a multidimensional pair-type local experiment, with compactness and a smaller-order prior or variational term controlling boundary selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform asymptotic minimax theorem establishing or refuting J R*(J,s_J) tending to min(rho,1/2), together with a Kuratowski or Hausdorff characterization of finite-minimizer accumulation sets and a second-order selection functional for critical sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames sharp minimax analysis through the distinction between procedures hidden by first-order equivalence and uses a second-order expansion to expose that distinction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Joint design-estimator choice needs a robust benchmark -> first-order risk makes competing procedures look alike -> second-order analysis reveals optimizer selection -> bounded pair mismatch creates a phase transition with a nontrivial limiting face

method_exemplars.technique: Construct shrinking least-favourable priors, apply a van Trees lower bound, and match a second-order local-risk expansion to an explicit estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result must also go beyond a first-order minimax value and use local least-favourable experiments to select among a flat face of design measures.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit bounded-outcome endpoint geometry, symmetric extreme schedules, and nonlinear shrinkage to match design-estimator upper bounds with Bayes lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its bounded finite-population loss is the closest unrestricted endpoint, while the mismatch class changes the least-favourable schedules and permits paired mass to become optimal.

open_problems.open_problem: Can SATE randomization tests be inverted exactly with finite-sample uniform coverage under every minimax-optimal bounded-mismatch assignment law, including correlated essentially noncanonical laws rather than only within-pair coin flips or product Bernoulli assignment?

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies inference for its minimax-optimal nonlinear procedure as an open problem and suggests inversion of randomization tests for weak nulls.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Exact binary matched-pair ATE inference reduces the worst compatible allocation to one boundary corner, but assumes a fixed within-pair coin flip.
source_refs.author: Bob Wilson

source_refs.claim: Exact binary ATE intervals need only O(log n) randomization tests for balanced Bernoulli and matched-pair designs, while other assignment mechanisms have different complexity.
source_refs.author: Peng Zhang

source_refs.claim: For general stratified binary experiments, exact conservative ATE inference maximizes a permutation p-value over compatible potential-outcome tables, with substantial product-form computational burden.
source_refs.author: Jiaxun Li, Jacob Spertus, and Philip B. Stark

source_refs.excerpt: The finite algorithm must return interval endpoints and a dual mixture on globally compatible completions.
There is no finite-sample coverage claim, no universal interval-shortening claim.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Wilson's boundary-corner proof and Zhang's fast algorithms exploit product or independent within-pair assignment structure. An essentially noncanonical minimax law may correlate assignments across pairs and place unequal mass on pair-assignment orbits, destroying the binomial or Poisson-binomial ordering that identifies a single worst compatible schedule. Li–Spertus–Stark show that even ordinary stratification restores a costly composite maximization, while the prior MRD and binary-truth-bound projects respectively leave completion-cell certification and finite-sample coverage unresolved. The first failed proof step is therefore stochastic monotonicity of the compatible-null p-value; it must be replaced by an exact orbit-level optimization that also respects the global mismatch cap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite-randomization test family and inversion algorithm with coverage uniform over all binary schedules satisfying the mismatch budget for each law on the optimal face, plus an orbit characterization of the worst compatible null and either a polynomial complexity bound or a matching impossibility theorem.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates exact inference through the combinatorial nuisance created by heterogeneous binary effects and converts that nuisance into a concrete worst-pattern problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Binary heterogeneous effects make weak-null inversion combinatorial -> matched-pair symmetry collapses compatible schedules -> monotonicity locates one worst corner -> noncanonical laws require a new orbit-level worst-null characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Index compatible sharp nulls by discordance counts, prove boundary monotonicity of exact tails, locate the worst null at an explicit corner, and invert by binary search.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired confidence set has the same fixed-population binary SATE target and composite-null obstacle, but orbit probabilities must replace the within-pair binomial tail.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse tests across adjacent effect tables and evaluate exact Poisson-binomial tails efficiently, with lower bounds on the required number of tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite optimal-law orbit distributions may permit analogous generating-function evaluation and p-value reuse even when independence is absent.

method_exemplars.technique: Maximize randomization p-values over compatible stratum-level tables using pruned combinatorial search and prove coverage after combining stratum information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The hard pair-mismatch budget similarly couples low-dimensional pair tables, making this the closest fallback when a one-corner reduction fails.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct, or rule out, an infinite sequence of bounded pair-mismatch instances on which essentially noncanonical designs beat every paired/iid-Bernoulli canonical mixture by a certified nonvanishing smaller-order risk gap.

source_refs.excerpt: Add a parameterized nondegenerate family ... with a proved positive correlated-design gap.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior reviewer identified the weakness of a lone rational separation witness and required a parameterized family. In the pair-mismatch problem, directly replicating a small noncanonical certificate need not preserve the global SATE normalization, the hard cap of s discordant pairs, or optimality against arbitrary estimators. The first proof step that changes is a composition or hard-budget-conditioning lemma showing how primal procedures and least-favourable priors tensorize or couple while retaining the global discordance constraint. Without such a lemma, the reported J=2 separation cannot establish persistence, its asymptotic order, or a genuine noncanonical regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit sequence (J,s_J), noncanonical assignment-estimator procedures, and matching rational dual priors proving a positive limit or sharp positive constant for a rescaled gap between unrestricted minimax risk and the best canonical-mixture risk, or a theorem proving that every such gap vanishes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its formulation makes the necessity of mixed-strategy randomization a structural design question rather than a numerical curiosity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Structured outcome classes alter minimax assignment -> optimality may require mixing beyond a single partition -> bounded pair mismatch asks whether genuinely noncanonical mixing has a persistent risk advantage

method_exemplars.technique: Match nonlinear endpoint estimators to least-favourable-prior lower bounds rather than comparing variances of fixed estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The claimed separation must survive optimization over every estimator on both the canonical and unrestricted sides.

method_exemplars.technique: Use symmetry averaging and bounded-outcome endpoint schedules to compare unrestricted assignment-estimator procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest proof template for removing label-specific procedures before comparing a canonical hull with the full invariant face.

literature_map:
Bai (2022, AER, arXiv:2206.07845) proves matched-pair optimality within stratified half-treatment designs under a superpopulation precision criterion.
Bai (2023, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.10.009) proves minimaxity from exact permutation invariance and explicitly leaves approximate invariance open.
Kallus (2018, JRSSB, arXiv:1312.0531) derives kernel allocation and pair matching from structured conditional-mean classes, while complete randomization is minimax without structure.
Kallus (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:2005.03151) shows mixed-strategy randomization can be required and introduces inference-constrained minimax design, but does not optimize unrestricted nonlinear estimators.
Morgan and Rubin (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1207.5625) formalize rerandomization for covariate balance rather than a hard restriction on pairwise potential-outcome mismatch.
Banerjee, Chassang, Montero, and Snowberg (2020, AER, DOI 10.1257/aer.20171634) formalize a balance-versus-robustness tradeoff under ambiguity preferences rather than an exact finite schedule class.
Harshaw, Sävje, Spielman, and Zhang (2024, JASA, arXiv:1911.03071) obtain MSE bounds and asymptotic normality for Gram–Schmidt Walk balance designs using operator-norm robustness.
de Chaisemartin (2021/2024, arXiv:2105.08766) derives minimax linear weighting under bounded treatment effects while fixing group-level unbiased estimators.
Hull (2026, arXiv:2608.09812) finds iid assignment optimal for unrestricted bounded schedules and a factor-two worst-case loss for paired randomization, creating an endpoint tension for mismatch-budget models.
Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2608.13822) solve unrestricted binary joint design-estimation using low-dimensional reduction, least-favourable priors, nonlinear shrinkage, and a second-order expansion; inference remains open.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015, Statistics in Medicine, DOI 10.1002/sim.6384), Aronow–Chang–Lopatto (2023), and Li–Spertus–Stark (2025, arXiv:2508.03834) show that exact binary weak-null inversion is possible but sensitive to assignment structure.
Zhang (2026, arXiv:2602.20498) and Wilson (2026, arXiv:2609.03227) obtain fast exact inversion for Bernoulli or within-pair coin-flip laws; neither covers correlated noncanonical laws.
The scan found no paper imposing a hard armwise-discordant-pair budget while jointly optimizing every assignment law and measurable SATE estimator.
It likewise found no classification of the resulting finite or limiting optimal faces or exact inversion procedure valid across a noncanonical optimal face.
